content.study:
Article 132A (“Constitutional validity of State laws not to be considered in proceedings under article 32”) of the Constitution of India has been omitted by constitutional amendment.

Status: Repealed / Omitted.
It is not current working law in the territory of India.

Examination Instruction:
When answering university or judicial service questions, note that Article 132A is omitted and identify the living constitutional or statutory provision that currently governs the subject matter.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the constitutional status and historical context of Article 132A (Constitutional validity of State laws not to be considered in proceedings under article 32).
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. INTRODUCTION & STATUS
Article 132A of the Constitution of India (“Constitutional validity of State laws not to be considered in proceedings under article 32”) is omitted. It does not form part of the living, enforceable constitutional text.

II. HISTORICAL BACKGROUND
The provision was repealed/omitted by constitutional amendment to remove obsolete structures, harmonize constitutional governance, or eliminate transitional provisions.

III. CURRENT GOVERNING HEADING
Examinees must identify the living provision that now regulates this field (e.g. general powers of Parliament, corresponding statutory enactments, or alternative constitutional mechanisms).

IV. CONCLUSION
Cite Article 132A strictly as a repealed/omitted heading. Do not apply its text to contemporary 2026 dispute scenarios.
